title: POST /api/events: browser event batch ingest
notes: Scenario: R's shared demo set. Tab IDs come from apps/api/app/engine/fixtures/demo_tabs.json (the 28 tabs in snapshot.example.json); project, claim, note and saved-context IDs come from grove.example.json and memory-search.example.json. IDs these examples create are listed in `introduces`; IDs that belong to another user are listed in `unknown_ids`.
Every request carries Authorization: Bearer <token> unless the example lists request.headers explicitly. user_id never appears in a request body; the server takes it from the token.
Durations are integer milliseconds (active_ms) so every sum is exact; the UI converts to minutes. Times are UTC and follow R's story clock (snapshot at 2026-10-04T11:40:00Z).
Errors are RFC 7807 problem JSON with `instance` = the request path, as in R's files.
batch_request and batch_response at the top level are the first_send example, kept for D's mock API test (apps/extension/tests/mock-api.test.mjs).
A batch holds 1 to 500 events; an empty list or more than 500 returns 422. type is OPEN, FOCUS, BLUR, UPDATE, CLOSE, IDLE or ACTIVE (stored as browser_events.event_type).

Fields by type. Every event: event_id, ts, type, tab_ref. OPEN adds domain, title, opener_tab_ref, dup_key, search_query. UPDATE adds domain, title, dup_key, search_query. FOCUS adds previous_tab_ref. BLUR adds active_ms. CLOSE, IDLE and ACTIVE add nothing. A listed field may be null; unknown fields return 422.
IDLE and ACTIVE carry the tab_ref of the focused tab, because browser_events.tab_ref is NOT NULL. active_ms on BLUR is focused time since the tab's FOCUS minus idle time.

event_id is minted on the device once, when the event is created; a retry resends the same event_id and ts. Inserts use ON CONFLICT (user_id, ts, event_id) DO NOTHING, so accepted + duplicates always equals the number of events sent.

title is at most 300 characters and redacted on the device. There is no URL field. dup_key is opaque to the server: 64 lowercase hex characters (SHA-256 of the normalized URL, computed on the device).
The server builds sessions from ts with the 30-minute gap rule, so late or out-of-order batches land in the right session. session_hint (SPEC §10.1) is optional and ignored.
is_tab_switch is set by the server: true when a FOCUS event has a previous_tab_ref different from its tab_ref.

This batch is the start of the late session (10:57:40 to 11:24:49): the refresh-token searches, the Medium and dev.to articles, the duplicate FastAPI tab and the two Rust sprout tabs. Tab 29 is a fourth search (query family qf_...001) that was closed at 11:11:22.
429 and 503 carry Retry-After in seconds. The extension keeps a batch in its queue until it gets a 202.
